title: Upper Log-Log Density: Sequences with Mertens-Scale Growth
content: The 'upper log-log density' of a sequence A = {a₁ < a₂ < ...} is defined as limsup_{x→∞} (1/log log x) * ∑_{aₙ ≤ x} 1/aₙ. This measures whether the reciprocal partial sums of A grow at the same rate as the prime reciprocal sums. By Mertens' second theorem, ∑_{p ≤ x} 1/p = log log x + M + O(1/log x), where M ≈ 0.2615 is the Meissel-Mertens constant. Thus the primes have upper log-log density exactly 1. A sequence has positive upper log-log density iff it is 'as dense as a positive fraction of the primes' in a harmonic-measure sense—a much weaker condition than having positive natural density or even positive upper Banach density.
mathContext: $\overline{d}_{\ell\ell}(A) = \limsup_{x\to\infty} \frac{1}{\log\log x}\sum_{a_n \leq x} \frac{1}{a_n}$. Mertens' 2nd theorem: $\sum_{p \leq x} \frac{1}{p} = \log\log x + M + O(1/\log x)$, where $M \approx 0.2615$. Primes: $\overline{d}_{\ell\ell}(\mathbb{P}) = 1$. For $A = \{n^2 : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$: $\sum_{n^2 \leq x} 1/n^2 \to \pi^2/6$ (constant), so $\overline{d}_{\ell\ell}(A) = 0$.

title: Primitive Sets and Erdős's 1935 Density Bound
content: A set A ⊆ ℕ is primitive if no element divides another: a_m ∤ a_n for all distinct m,n. The primes form a primitive set (no prime divides another). Erdős proved (1935) that for any primitive set A, ∑_{a ∈ A} 1/(a log a) ≤ C for an absolute constant C. This upper bound shows that primitive sets cannot be 'too dense'—the harmonic sums weighted by 1/log are bounded. The connection to Problem #1217: if one wants to extract a primitive subsequence from A while preserving positive log-log density, one must navigate this Erdős bound. For sequences with ∑ 1/aₙ ~ C log log x, extracting a primitive subsequence typically loses at most a constant factor.
mathContext: Erdős 1935: For any primitive set $A$, $\sum_{a \in A} \frac{1}{a \log a} \leq C_0$ (absolute constant). Equivalently: $\sum_{a \in A, a \leq x} \frac{1}{a} = O(\log x)$. Primes: $\sum_{p \leq x} \frac{1}{p \log p} \approx \int_2^x \frac{dt}{t (\log t)^2} = O(1)$ (converges).
prerequisites: prime set as canonical primitive set

title: Erdős-Sárközy-Sós 1966: Density and Structure Theorems
content: The [ESS66] reference is Erdős, Sárközy, and Sós, 1966. This collaboration produced several fundamental results in additive combinatorics and analytic number theory. Their 1966 work spans topics including: (1) multiplicatively structured sets and their densities; (2) sum-free sets in arithmetic progressions; (3) Sidon sets (B₂ sets) and their maximal density; (4) sequences with the 'Property P' (no element is a sum of two others). In the context of Problem #1217, [ESS66] proved a density-preservation theorem: sequences with positive upper log-log density contain subsequences with the same density and some additional algebraic property. The exact form depends on which 1966 paper is referenced.
mathContext: ESS66 result (reconstructed): If $A$ has $\overline{d}_{\ell\ell}(A) > 0$, then $A$ contains a subsequence $B$ with $\overline{d}_{\ell\ell}(B) > 0$ and $B$ satisfying a structural property (primitive / sum-free / Sidon). The exact statement requires consulting the original paper; the source for Problem #1217 is corrupted.

title: Lean Formalization: Filter.limsup and Analytic Number Theory
content: The placeholder `erdos_1217 : True := by sorry` requires formalization infrastructure only partially available in Mathlib. Key components: (1) `Filter.limsup` for the limsup of the reciprocal sum as a function of x; (2) `Finset.sum` over elements ≤ x for the partial sums; (3) Mertens' second theorem (∑_{p ≤ x} 1/p ~ log log x) for the density normalization—not yet in Mathlib; (4) extracting a structurally constrained subsequence while preserving density, which involves Ramsey-type or greedy arguments at the analytic number theory level.
mathContext: Lean 4 sketch: `def loglogDensity (A : ℕ → ℕ) : ℝ := Filter.limsup (fun x => (Real.log (Real.log x))⁻¹ * ∑ n in Finset.filter (fun n => A n ≤ x) Finset.univ, (A n : ℝ)⁻¹) Filter.atTop`. The `Filter.limsup` in Mathlib 4 operates on `Filter`s and requires a `ConditionallyCompleteLattice` structure on the codomain.
